cross_cutting.content:
# Product brief: RuFlo AI Team and MCP Launch Doctor

Status: input to ADR-351 (downstream products that consume ruvector edge services) Source: product research supplied by rUv, 2026-09-29. Marketplace figures were observed by the author in the live Claude directory and are not independently re-verified here.

## Thesis

The strongest opportunity is not another generic connector. It is a packaged "AI team" product built on RuFlo Federation, Cognitum, and ruOS.

Give Claude a team, a shared control room, and a computer when the work requires one.

## Marketplace observations (author-reported)

- The directory showed 3,841 connectors. Discovery is dominated by systems of record: Google Drive, Gmail, Calendar, Microsoft 365, Notion, Figma, Slack, Atlassian, HubSpot, Asana and Linear.
- Popular plugins include Notion, Canva, Linear, Carta and Anthropic's vertical workflow bundles. Trending: financial-advisor platforms, legal research, Amazon selling, jobs and consumer services.
- Plugins (skills + MCP services + interactive MCP Apps) are now the main third-party extension format: https://claude.com/blog/build-plugins-for-claude
- MCP Apps render dashboards, forms and live interfaces inline: https://blog.modelcontextprotocol.io/posts/2026-01-26-mcp-apps/
- Search gaps (semantic matching, so counts are directional, medium confidence): "AI chief of staff" 0; "business operating system" 7; "agent cost tracking" 10; "fleet" 24; "agent evaluation" 26 (Langfuse, DeepEval, MLflow, Coval); "multi-agent team" 33, few providing a visible, general-purpose team.

## Flagship: RuFlo AI Team

A user describes an outcome. The plugin creates a small specialist team, assigns work, prevents duplicate effort, tracks budget and risk, and shows progress in an interactive control room. It sells an outcome, not "multi-agent infrastructure".

Layer | Provides 
---|---
RuFlo | agents, claims, messaging, workflows, signed evidence 
Cognitum | durable memory, evaluation, cost accounting, policy, security events 
ruOS | isolated desktop for browser/GUI work 
MCP App | live Kanban, agent activity, approvals, evidence, spend 
Agent Skills | research, release preparation, security review, business ops 

Initial experience:

- "Research this market and produce a launch plan."
- Claude proposes a three-agent team and a declared budget.
- User approves.
- Inline control room shows assignments, progress, cost and evidence.
- Agents request explicit approval before external writes or desktop actions.
- The run produces a signed, shareable result page and a reusable template (the viral loop: recipients inspect evidence, fork, start their own team).

## Opportunity ranking

Product | Unique | Fast to ship | Viral | Review fit | Recommendation 
---|---|---|---|---|---
RuFlo AI Team | 5 | 4 | 5 | 4 | Flagship 
MCP Launch Doctor | 5 | 5 | 4 | 5 | Fastest launch 
Agent Flight Recorder | 4 | 4 | 4 | 4 | Enterprise add-on 
Business Control Room | 4 | 3 | 5 | 3 | Expand later 
Cognitum Fleet Doctor | 3 | 4 | 2 | 4 | Strong vertical 

## Fast wedge: MCP Launch Doctor

Turn an API or MCP repository into a secure, directory-ready Claude plugin.

- Audit tool names, descriptions and annotations.
- Validate OAuth and RFC 9728 discovery.
- Detect secret-bearing schemas and prompt-injection risks.
- Generate review tests, listing copy, icons, legal checklists, submission bundles.
- Produce a shareable readiness scorecard.

Builds largely on existing assets:chatgpt-mcp-studio-site, the security
harness, submission skills, and the RuFlo review work. No clear marketplace
leader exists for end-to-end MCP directory validation, and the directory
policy (accurate behavior, helpful errors, frugal outputs, OAuth, explicit
annotations) makes it timely:
https://support.claude.com/en/articles/13145358-anthropic-software-directory-policy

## Freemium model (RuFlo AI Team)

Free: one team at a time, up to three agents, one metered ruOS machine, a monthly allowance of agent/model/desktop units, public or private signed result pages, no card required.

Paid: larger teams and concurrent runs, persistent Cognitum memory, scheduled operations, private templates and longer retention, higher budgets, evaluations, policy gates, audit exports.

Charge against unified "work units" (model tokens, machine time, storage, external API cost). Set the free allowance from measured p50/p95 run cost, not an arbitrary number.

## Approval-safe design

- External writes are approval-gated.
- Never transfer money or financial assets.
- No advertising or sponsored results.
- Narrow, factual tools; first-party RuFlo/Cognitum/ruOS APIs.
- Fence third-party and agent-generated content as untrusted data.
- Never read Claude memory or unrelated conversation data.
- Explicit boolean tool annotations and accurate OAuth challenges.
- Public sharing is opt-in with a redaction preview.
- The free machine is isolated, disposable and resource-capped.

## Recommended sequence

- Package the existing RuFlo connector with 4-6 team-workflow skills.
- Add a cross-platform MCP App control-room UI.
- Add Cognitum cost, evaluation and security receipts.
- Attach the metered free ruOS desktop only when a task needs a computer.
- Add signed, redacted, forkable result pages.
- Beta-test three workflows: market research, release preparation, security audit.
- Submit as "RuFlo AI Team", not as infrastructure.

Evidence quality: marketplace composition and policies high confidence; search-gap counts medium; virality is a product hypothesis.

## How ruvector edge services support this (to be reflected in ADR-351)

Product need | Edge service 
---|---
Accurate OAuth + RFC 9728 challenges for every MCP surface | ruvector-edge-auth (resource-bound tokens, AS + PR metadata) 
Launch Doctor's OAuth/9728 validator | reuses the edge-auth conformance tests as a checker 
Durable team memory, recall, evidence search | vector / quantized collections, one DO per tenant collection 
Signed, shareable, forkable result pages | RVF export with witness chain, served read-only per tenant 
Work-unit metering and free-tier caps | per-tenant quota and usage counters in the edge core 
Control-room MCP App | MCP endpoint behind edge-auth, tenant-scoped

cross_cutting.content:
# AI Product GTM

Go-to-market strategy for AI products. These aren't generic AI principles — they're patterns from selling autonomous AI agents into enterprises where "autonomous" scared buyers and "teammate" converted them.

## When to Use

Triggers:

- "How do we position this AI product?"
- "Buyers say they're worried about AI breaking production"
- "Should we call it autonomous or copilot?"
- "How do we price AI when usage varies 10x by customer?"
- "Enterprise security passed but ops rejected us — why?"

Context:

- AI agent platforms (coding, support, ops)
- LLM-based applications
- Autonomous tools that do things (not just suggest)
- AI infrastructure
- Anything where the AI makes decisions

## Core Frameworks

### 1. The Real Enterprise AI Objection (It's Not What You Think)

What I Learned Selling Autonomous AI Agents:

Three months in, enterprise security reviews were passing fast. Good sign, right? Then the pattern emerged: security approved, but operations rejected us.

The objection wasn't "will the AI break production?" — they assumed it would break production eventually. The real question was:

"Who's responsible when the agent does something wrong?"

Not "do we trust the agent?" — "do we trust our team to handle this?"

Why This Matters:

Autonomous agents create a new operational burden. You're not selling AI capability, you're selling organizational readiness. When your agent halts production at 2am, who gets paged? Who fixes it? Who explains it to the VP?

Framework: The Accountability Cascade

Before deploying AI agents, enterprises need clear answers:

- L1 Response: Who monitors the agent? (24/7 ops team, or dev team on-call?)
- L2 Escalation: When agent action fails, who debugs? (Agent team, or product team?)
- L3 Ownership: When something breaks badly, who owns customer communication?

If you can't answer all three, they won't buy. Doesn't matter how good your AI is.

How This Changes Your Sales Process:

Old approach:

- Demo the AI
- Show accuracy metrics
- Talk about ROI

New approach:

- Demo the AI
- Show the failure modes explicitly
- Ask: "Who on your team would handle this scenario?"
- Walk through their incident response process
- Map AI failures to their existing runbooks

The Qualification Question:

"Walk me through what happens when the agent takes an action that breaks a workflow. Who gets alerted? Who investigates? Who decides whether to roll back or fix forward?"

If they can't answer, they're not ready. Pause the deal and help them build the process first.

Common Mistake:

Treating this as a product objection ("we'll make the AI more accurate"). It's an organizational objection. More accuracy doesn't solve "who owns this at 2am?"

Pattern I've Seen Work:

Companies that succeed with AI agents already have:

- On-call rotations for production systems
- Incident response playbooks
- Blameless postmortem culture
- Clear escalation paths

Companies that struggle:

- Manual deployment processes
- Hero culture ("Steve fixes everything")
- No formal incident response
- Blame-focused culture

Decision Criteria:

Before demoing autonomous AI to enterprises, ask yourself: "If this breaks their production, who on their team owns the fix?" If you can't answer, they can't buy.

### 2. Copilot vs Agent vs Teammate (Three Different GTM Motions)

The Positioning Trap:

Early enterprise conversations, we positioned as "autonomous AI agent." Buyers flinched. One word change — "autonomous" → "AI teammate" — and deal progression improved measurably.

Why? Word choice shapes buyer psychology.

The Three Framings:

1. Copilot (Safest, Lowest Value)

- What it means: AI suggests, human decides every time
- Buyer psychology: Feels safe, non-threatening
- GTM motion: Developer adoption, bottoms-up
- Use case: Code completion, writing assistance, search
- Objection: "Is this worth paying for?" (low perceived value)

2. Agent (Scariest, Highest Value)

- What it means: AI acts autonomously, human reviews periodically
- Buyer psychology: Scary, implies replacing humans
- GTM motion: Enterprise sales, top-down
- Use case: Batch processing, automated workflows, ops
- Objection: "What if it breaks production?" (accountability fear)

3. Teammate (Sweet Spot)

- What it means: AI and human collaborate, split the work
- Buyer psychology: Partnership, not replacement
- GTM motion: Hybrid (dev adoption + manager approval)
- Use case: Most AI agent platforms
- Objection: "How do we integrate this into our workflow?" (process question)

The Positioning Shift:

Before: "Autonomous AI agent that handles complex workflows end-to-end"

- Developers: "Cool, but scary"
- Managers: "Will this replace our team?"
- Deal progression: Slow

After: "AI teammate that pairs with your engineers on complex tasks"

- Developers: "This helps me"
- Managers: "This makes my team more productive"
- Deal progression: Three enterprise deals that had stalled 4+ months closed within 8 weeks of the shift

Specific Language Choices That Mattered:

❌ Don't say:

- "Autonomous" (scary)
- "Replaces" (threatening)
- "Fully automated" (no control)
- "AI-first" (what does that even mean?)

✅ Do say:

- "Teammate" (collaborative)
- "Augments" or "Accelerates" (helping, not replacing)
- "You stay in control" (reassuring)
- "Handles the repetitive work" (specific value)

How to Choose Your Framing:
Does your AI make decisions without human approval?
├─ Yes → Are you selling to developers or enterprises?
│   ├─ Developers → "Agent" framing (they want autonomous)
│   └─ Enterprises → "Teammate" framing (they want control)
└─ No → "Copilot" framing (augmentation, not automation)

The Hard Truth:

You can build an agent but position it as a copilot. You can't build a copilot and position it as an agent. Product capabilities set a ceiling, positioning chooses where you land below it.

Common Mistake:

Using "autonomous" because it sounds impressive. Impressive ≠ trusted. If buyers flinch at your positioning, you've lost them.

### 3. The AI Pricing Problem (When Usage Varies 10x)

The Pattern:

Every AI company I've worked with faces this: Customer A uses 1,000 API calls/month. Customer B uses 10,000. Do you charge Customer B 10x more? If yes, they churn. If no, your margins collapse.

The Three Models:

1. Seat-Based ($X per user/month)

- When it works: AI augments human work predictably
- Example: Code completion, writing assistant
- Problem: Doesn't capture AI value scaling
- Real risk: High-usage customers are your best customers, but they subsidize low-usage ones

2. Usage-Based ($X per API call / prediction / hour)

- When it works: AI does variable work, customers understand the unit
- Example: Image generation, transcription, batch ML
- Problem: Sticker shock for high-usage customers
- Real risk: Customers optimize to use less of your product

3. Outcome-Based ($X per outcome achieved)

- When it works: You can measure outcomes reliably
- Example: "Pay per bug fixed" or "Pay per support ticket resolved"
- Problem: Hard to measure, easy to game
- Real risk: You bear all the risk if AI doesn't perform

What Actually Works (Hybrid):

Base fee (covers fixed costs) + variable fee (scales with value).

Example structure:

- Base: $X/month per team (access to platform)
- Variable: $Y per successful action/outcome
- Why this works:
- Base covers infra/support costs
- Variable aligns with customer value
- High-usage customers aren't punished (they're getting more value)

The Pricing Conversation I Wish I'd Had Earlier:

When pricing usage-based AI:

Ask the customer: "How much would it cost you to do this manually?"

If it's $0.10 per API call but saves them $2 in labor, you're underpriced. If it costs $0.50 per call but saves them $0.40, they won't use it enough to matter.

Pricing Rule:

Your variable cost should be 20-30% of customer's alternative cost. High enough to capture value, low enough that they'll use it liberally.

Common Mistake:

Copying OpenAI's pricing ($0.01 per 1K tokens) because "that's what everyone does." Your cost structure isn't OpenAI's cost structure. Your value isn't OpenAI's value. Price for your business.

### 4. The AI Trust Ladder (From Someone Who Climbed It)

The Pattern:

You can't sell AI by saying "trust us, it works." You build trust in stages.

First: Transparency (Before First Demo)

Send these three docs before they ask:

- Model card (what model, trained on what, accuracy on what benchmarks)
- Security whitepaper (where data goes, how it's processed)
- Explainability doc (how to interpret AI decisions)

Why this works: Buyers expect to do diligence. If you send docs before they ask, you look confident and credible.

Second: Control (In the Demo)

Show them the safety mechanisms:

- How users approve/reject AI suggestions
- Kill switches and rollback mechanisms
- Confidence scores and when AI says "I'm not sure"

Why this works: Fear of "runaway AI" is real. Showing control mechanisms proves you thought about failure modes.

Third: Performance (Week 4-8)

Prove it works:

- Benchmarks vs baseline (human or previous tool)
- Case study from similar company
- Live demo on their data (if possible)

Why this works: Proof beats promises. One customer saying "we saved X hours/week" is worth 100 marketing claims.

Fourth: Scale (When They're Serious)

Show enterprise readiness:

- Enterprise deployment examples
- Performance at scale (latency, throughput, error rates)
- Compliance docs (SOC 2, GDPR, etc.)

Why this works: Enterprises don't deploy MVPs. They need proof you won't fall over at 1000 users.

The Mistake I Made:

Trying to prove performance before explaining how the AI worked. Buyers didn't trust the benchmarks because they didn't understand the system. Order matters.

Decision Criteria:

If buyers ask "how does this work?" before you've demoed, you skipped transparency. Back up and send the docs.

## Web Summit Breakout Startup Samepage.ai Launches Bets, an Operating System for AI-Era Product Teams

Humans and agents work together to discover, build, and take product to market

LISBON, Portugal, Nov. 9, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Samepage.ai today launched Samepage Bets, an operating system for product teams in the AI era. One of 15 Web Summit 2026 breakout startups, Samepage will show Bets publicly for the first time on Centre Stage on Wednesday, Nov. 11, before more than 70,000 attendees.

AI made building fast. Samepage Bets helps teams build the right thing: agents do the work, humans make the calls.

AI has made software faster and cheaper to build, raising the stakes on one question: what should we build next? The answer is scattered across sales calls, CRM records, support tickets, competitor launches, and internal chat.

Bets brings that work onto one board. An Insights Inbox automatically triages feature requests, bugs, competitor moves, and evidence from more than 50 native integrations across CRM, call recordings, support, the web, and internal communication. Each insight can become a bet that moves through three stages:

- Planning: Research and requirements agents build the case, backed by customer evidence and a priority score.
- Building: Prototyping and coding agents work in the team's codebase and open pull requests in GitHub.
- Go-to-maket: A product marketing agent publishes release notes to Notion and support articles to Intercom.

Bets is also multiplayer: engineering, product marketing, and other partners stay on the same page from one board.

"AI made building fast. Now the hard part is making sure you're building the right thing," said Sahil Jain, co-founder and CEO of Samepage. "Bets gives product teams one place where agents do the heavy lifting and humans make the calls, from the first customer signal all the way to launch."

Bets builds on Samepage Signals, launched in June alongside $4.85 million in seed funding. Signals surfaced the insights; Bets turns them into a launched product.

"I built something like this for myself in Claude. Samepage Bets thought of things I hadn't, and gives our team a consistent flow," said Ben Silver, head of product at MCL Finance.

"We could have pieced something together in Claude, but we'd have ended up maintaining a tool instead of building our product," said Nick Reid, head of product and AI operations at Customer Alliance.

Samepage Bets is available today, and teams can get started for free at samepage.ai.

About Samepage

Samepage is the operating system for product teams in the AI era. Its flagship product, Samepage Bets, brings humans and agents together to discover, build, and launch product across more than 50 native integrations. Founded by the team behind AdStage, Samepage is backed by Craft Ventures, Freestyle VC, and Glasswing Ventures. Learn more at samepage.ai.

cross_cutting.content:
# Automattic launches Spacefast, a company that deploys apps built with the AI tools people already use

Automattic on November 9, 2026 launched Spacefast as a new company that, it says, gives an AI agent a head start and then puts the resulting website or app online with a private link a team can comment on. The announcement was issued as an Automattic press release on PR Newswire at 9:00 a.m. Eastern Time and reported the same day by Ivan Mehta at TechCrunch. People keep working in the AI tools they already use, the release says, including ChatGPT, Claude, Muse, Grok Bot, OpenClaw, Hermes and coding agents such as Claude Code, Codex and Cursor.

Spacefast is led by Batuhan İçöz, whom the release names as founder and chief executive. İçöz joined Automattic through its acquisition of Texts and built the first version on his own during Radical Speed Month, an internal program that gave staff time to focus on a single project. As colleagues joined in, Automattic made the project its own company. TechCrunch, citing an interview with İçöz, says he had been working on Automattic's messaging app Beeper at the time, often received preview links from non-technical friends who were trying out AI-built sites, and first called the project Stattic. The service was soft-launched in September to gather feedback before today's public launch.

The release describes a different approach from AI website builders that ask users to switch to a bundled model and pay for it a second time. Spacefast is meant to work with the agent a person already pays for, supply expert starting decisions and a ready database, then publish a private URL from the chat. Built-in application authentication, transactional email and shared team knowledge, including playbooks, past decisions and brand context, are described as arriving in the coming weeks. Teams can comment on the live page and ask the agent to turn those comments into fixes. Supported stacks named in the release include Vite, TanStack Start, Next.js and Astro. There is also a dashboard, command-line tool, application programming interface and Model Context Protocol server, according to the company's about page.

Spacefast runs on WordPress.com infrastructure, which Automattic says handles more than 15 billion page views a month. WordPress VIP and Pressable customers, the release says, do not have to approve a new vendor and can connect Spacefast to a site they already run. İçöz is quoted saying that AI is turning everyone into a maker and that the web is about to feel like its early days again, full of small personal things people build for themselves, their teams and their friends. TechCrunch notes that the product competes with services such as Lovable and Emergent, but aims to remain more open about which agent the user brings.

Pricing in the release starts with a free tier. Personal plans include one dollar a month of usage for free, with custom domains and a built-in database. The Go plan, at five dollars a month, adds unlimited spaces and more usage. The Pro plan, at fifteen dollars a month per member, adds team features and early access to new capabilities. Enterprise plans are available with custom pricing. Official plugins are listed for Claude, ChatGPT and Grok Bot, and any other agent can connect through the API, CLI and MCP.

The launch language is promotional, and several advertised capabilities are still on the way rather than shipping today. TechCrunch also places the debut against a turbulent period at Automattic, including a brief boardroom fight over chief executive Matt Mullenweg and reported layoffs, context that is independent of the product claims. The existence of the public launch, the named leadership, the bring-your-own-agent pitch and the published price list are established by Automattic's own release and corroborated by TechCrunch's report.

# (2nd LD) Nvidia, SKT, Rebellions to jointly establish heterogeneous computing system for AI

All News 18:47 November 09, 2026

(ATTN: ADDS more info in paras 9-10, new photo; RECASTS 3rd para)
By Kang Jae-eun

SEOUL, Nov. 9 (Yonhap) -- Nvidia Corp., SK Telecom Co. and domestic artificial intelligence (AI) chip startup Rebellions agreed Monday to combine their respective strengths to establish a heterogeneous computing system.

Under the trilateral memorandum of understanding (MOU), the companies will cooperate in the establishment of a heterogeneous AI computing system connecting Nvidia's graphic processing units (GPUs) with neural processing units (NPUs) designed by Rebellions that will be used in the building of SK Telecom AI data centers.

The tie-up will be based on the U.S. chipmaker's NVLink Fusion program.

The NVLink Fusion program allows hyperscalers and custom chip designers to integrate their own AI processors directly into Nvidia's rack-scale infrastructure.

The MOU was signed on the margins of AI Day Seoul, a tech event hosted by Nvidia that kicked off its two-day run in southern Seoul.

"Korea is a technology leader, and with AI being one of the fastest growing technologies that has ever happened ... this collaboration we are working on together, we believe, can help accelerate innovation in Korea," Jesse Clayton, the principal manager for AI infrastructure at Nvidia, said, at a media round table following the MOU's signing.

The MOU signed Monday came amid the support from South Korea's ministry of science and ICT.

The ministry expected the partnership to expand the scope of application for domestic advanced semiconductors, and provide opportunities for local companies in the global market.

Separately, Nvidia held a startup forum to explore business opportunities with more than 20 Korean startups in AI foundation models, physical AI, AI infrastructure and AI chips, in cooperation with the science ministry.

During the event, the U.S. chipmaker announced plans to invest in South Korean AI startup Point2 Technology, as well as additional investments in Motif Technologies, RLWRLD and Upstage.

Nvidia, however, declined to comment on the abrupt cancellation of a visit by Madison Huang, a senior director at Nvidia and daughter of Chief Executive Officer (CEO) Jensen Huang, as well as his alleged relationship with a suspected Chinese spy.

"It is not related to the event. We cannot answer because she (Madison) did not attend the event," an official from the U.S. chipmaker, said, during the media session.

It was in response to a question about whether the growing pressure from the U.S. Congress over Huang's scandal could affect Nvidia's partnerships with Samsung Electronics and SK hynix, and its scheduled delivery of GPUs to South Korea.

On Thursday (U.S. time), three Republican committee leaders requested Huang to sit for a closed-door briefing regarding his alleged relationship with a businesswoman reportedly identified as an intelligence asset for Beijing.

Subsequently, Nvidia said it opened an internal probe into the matter, following an email sent from Huang himself to employees admitting to being "unfaithful" to his wife and taking "full responsibility" for what he did.

cross_cutting.description: Infra and HUMAIN Sign Financing Agreements of up to SAR2.5 Billion to Advance Saudi Arabia’s AI Infrastructure ... today announced the signing of two financing agreements totaling up to SAR2.5 billion (approximately $667 million) to support artificial intelligence computing deployment and the development of critical power infrastructure in Saudi Arabia.
cross_cutting.content:
Monday 29 Jumada al-Ula 1448 - November 9, 2026

Infra and HUMAIN Sign Financing Agreements of up to SAR2.5 Billion to Advance Saudi Arabia’s AI Infrastructure

7 minutes ago

Voice reader

Riyadh, November 09, 2026, SPA -- The National Infrastructure Fund (“Infra”) and HUMAIN, a Public Investment Fund (PIF) company delivering full-stack artificial intelligence capabilities globally, today announced the signing of two financing agreements totaling up to SAR2.5 billion (approximately $667 million) to support artificial intelligence computing deployment and the development of critical power infrastructure in Saudi Arabia.

The agreements were signed on November 8 in Riyadh in the presence of Governor of PIF Yasir Al-Rumayyan, Minister of Economy and Planning and Chairman of Infra’s Board of Directors Faisal Alibrahim, and Governor of the National Development Fund Abdulaziz Alarifi.

The facilities are the first transactions announced under Infra’s AI Data Center Financing Program. They build on the strategic financing framework announced by Infra and HUMAIN at Davos in January 2026, which outlined non-binding financing terms of up to SAR4.5 billion ($1.2 billion) to support AI and digital infrastructure projects in the Kingdom.

The GPU financing facility, of up to SAR1.1 billion ($293.3 million), will support the procurement and deployment of graphics processing units (GPUs), representing approximately 25 MW of IT load.

A second facility of up to SAR1.4 billion ($373.3 million) will finance the development of substations, transmission infrastructure and grid connections to support HUMAIN’s AI data centers in Saudi Arabia. The planned power infrastructure is designed to support future data center development with up to 1 GW of IT capacity, helping create the conditions for investment by developers, hyperscalers and institutional investors.

“Through these agreements, we aim to unlock investment well beyond Infra’s own commitment. Supporting HUMAIN’s computing deployment alongside essential power infrastructure helps prepare a broader pipeline of data center projects for investment. Our role is to strengthen project readiness and bankability, with commercial viability and economic value guiding how we deploy our capital. This partnership connects our priorities with commercial discipline, helping build a financing market that can attract a broader pool of private and institutional capital and sustain the local AI infrastructure growth,” said CEO of Infra Eng. Esmail bin Mohammed Alsallom.

“AI infrastructure is becoming foundational to the next generation of computing, and scaling it requires both significant investment and the infrastructure to support it. These facilities with Infra will help accelerate the deployment of advanced computing capacity and the power infrastructure required to support it. At HUMAIN, we are focused on building and operating AI infrastructure at scale, while developing the technologies and platforms that enable organizations and customers globally to put AI to work,” said CEO of HUMAIN Tareq Amin.

-- SPA

cross_cutting.content:
# Nvidia, SKT and Rebellions team up to build Korean sovereign AI

## AI Summary Nvidia said on Nov. 9 it will work with Rebellions and SK Telecom on upgrading South Korea’s sovereign AI infrastructure based on NVLink Fusion. Rebellions will connect its Rivel R200 NPU to Nvidia’s platform using NVLink Fusion and an MGX rack architecture. The system is slated for SK Telecom AI data centres, with deployment planned from 2028. The companies will also develop distributed inference assigning GPUs to prefill and NPUs to decode.

- Writer Daegeon Seok
- published 2026-11-09 14:46:06
- updated 2026-11-09 14:53:15

[DigitalToday reporter Daegeon Seok] An AI chip designed in South Korea will be integrated into Nvidia rack-scale infrastructure. Nvidia said on Nov. 9 it is pursuing cooperation with Rebellions and SK Telecom to upgrade South Korea’s sovereign AI infrastructure based on NVLink Fusion. The three companies plan to combine Rebellions’ AI processors and SK Telecom’s data centre, model and service capabilities on Nvidia’s open infrastructure platform.

Rebellions will attach its Rivel R200 neural processing unit (NPU), a chip specialised for AI computation, to Nvidia’s platform using NVLink Fusion. NVLink Fusion is a technology that extends Nvidia’s high-bandwidth, low-latency scale-up networking to external custom chips. R200 units inside a rack will be linked with NVLink, and the system will be developed based on the MGX rack architecture.

Rivel R200, currently under development, targets low-latency, high-efficiency inference for advanced models such as mixture-of-experts (MoE) models with trillions of parameters. The completed system is set to be installed in SK Telecom’s AI data centres. Nvidia explained that GPU and NPU systems can share rack space, power supply and cooling design thanks to the MGX architecture. Rebellions will also use the MGX ecosystem’s ODM and components supply chain. The Rebellions R200 system is scheduled to be deployed from 2028.

The three companies will also develop a distributed inference approach that assigns the right processor to each stage of AI response generation. Under the configuration, Nvidia GPUs will handle prefill for input processing, while Rebellions NPUs will handle decode for output generation to improve throughput and power efficiency. SK Telecom plans to link this infrastructure with its own models including A.X K2, and with public services under the government’s Everyone’s AI project.

Rebellions CEO Seonghyeon Park (박성현) said the announcement is an important turning point for expanding South Korea’s sovereign AI ecosystem by combining Korean AI semiconductors and models with global technology. He said Rebellions will design next-generation AI infrastructure together with Nvidia and SKT, based on proprietary technology it has proven while growing as a South Korean AI chip company, and will work to make Korea-made technology a key axis driving global AI.

SK Telecom President and CEO Jaehun Jeong (정재헌) said the cooperation is meaningful because it demonstrates the potential of next-generation sovereign AI infrastructure by combining global AI infrastructure technology with domestic AI semiconductors. He said SK Telecom will strengthen full-stack sovereign AI competitiveness and contribute to the development of the domestic AI ecosystem by linking its AI data centres, its own AI models including A.X K2, and public-facing AI services developed through the Everyone’s AI project.

Nvidia founder and CEO Jensen Huang (젠슨 황) said South Korea has the talent, technology and industrial capabilities to emerge as a global leader in AI. He said NVLink Fusion will allow South Korean semiconductor companies to connect custom ASICs to Nvidia’s AI factory platform and run AI workloads by tightly integrating their own processors with Nvidia computing. He added that Nvidia is building a computing foundation with MSIT, Rebellions and SK Telecom so South Korea can produce its own intelligence and power the next industrial revolution.

cross_cutting.description: 2026 年 11 月 9 日，在日本， Stavian Corporation和Midas Capital Co., Ltd.签署了一份谅解备忘录 (MOU)，就投资和开发越南的海底光缆基础设施、数字技术基础设施以及人工智能(AI)和超级智能 (SI) 基础设施开展战略合作。
cross_cutting.content:
# Stavian Group 和 Midas Capital 签署了一份谅解备忘录，就投资和开发越南的海底光纤基础设施和数字技术基础设施开展战略合作。

在越南国家主席兼秘书长苏林的见证下，斯塔维安集团与迈达斯资本就合作投资开发越南海底光缆基础设施和数字技术/人工智能基础设施举行了签约仪式。

2026 年 11 月 9 日，在日本， Stavian Corporation和Midas Capital Co., Ltd.签署了一份谅解备忘录 (MOU)，就投资和开发越南的海底光缆基础设施、数字技术基础设施以及人工智能(AI)和超级智能 (SI) 基础设施开展战略合作。

此次签约仪式由越南国家主席兼秘书长苏林见证，体现了促进国际合作在发展高科技基础设施、加强互联互通和扩大资源以服务越南数字化转型进程方面的重要性。

根据谅解备忘录，双方同意建立长期战略合作框架，预计总投资额达10亿美元，重点关注四大领域：投资开发连接越南与国际社会及日本的海底光缆；开发数字技术基础设施、人工智能（AI）和系统集成（SI）基础设施，包括数据中心、数字科技园区以及AI和SI计算基础设施；对接金融资源和国际合作伙伴；技术转让、应用国际运营标准以及培养高素质人才。在该合作框架下，斯塔维安集团将在越南的项目开发和投资流程中发挥主导作用，而迈达斯资本将负责协调对接日本及国际上的金融资源、技术合作伙伴和相关机构。双方的目标是在评估、审核和后续实施协议的基础上，制定具体项目。

此次宣布的关键数字基础设施项目之一是MViSTA ，这是一个基于开放式连接模式的国际海底光缆系统，旨在连接越南与马来西亚、新加坡和泰国。该项目旨在提升国际传输能力，实现数据连接的多元化，并支持该地区数据中心生态系统、云计算和人工智能/系统集成（AI/SI）应用的发展。根据设计，MViSTA全长约2500公里，通过16对光纤实现400Tbps的传输容量。该项目吸引了来自四个国家的战略投资者：越南的Stavian集团、日本的Midas Capital、马来西亚的OMS集团和新加坡的LitUp。这将是一个满足日益增长的跨境数据流、云计算和人工智能/系统集成（AI/SI）应用需求的关键平台。

世界文化中心对平阳省的传统陶器村进行了调查。（DTTC）——世界工艺理事会（WCC）的一个国际专家代表团目前正在对平阳省（胡志明市）的陶瓷工艺村进行调查和评估。

黄金价格全面上涨，每两上涨100万越南盾。11月9日上午，越南国内黄金价格上涨100万越南盾/两。与此同时，国际黄金价格也上涨超过1%，报每盎司4129.69美元。

提高农业和畜牧业产量，并储备物资以满足年底购物需求。（调查）——河内及其他地区正在加紧农牧业生产和物资储备，以确保年末购物季和2027年农历新年期间的物资供应。预计消费需求将比平时增长约10-15%。

与MViSTA项目同步，斯塔维安集团（Stavian Group）正通过其旗下的斯塔维安高科技基础设施股份公司（Stavian Hightech）在胡志明市开发斯塔维安数字园区（Stavian DP） 。该项目规划占地约300公顷，旨在打造一个集中式数字技术园区，服务于大型云计算服务提供商、人工智能和系统集成数据中心以及需要数字基础设施的企业和机构。斯塔维安数字园区的可行性研究由美国贸易发展署（USTDA）资助，由高纬环球（Cushman & Wakefield）牵头，APTelecom作为专业电信分包商参与其中。

MViSTA和Stavian DP相辅相成，将国际传输基础设施与数据中心以及人工智能和系统集成计算基础设施能力连接起来。通过这两个项目，Stavian集团旨在按照国际标准构建一个同步、可扩展的数字基础设施生态系统，从而提升越南的互联互通水平，并促进越南的高科技发展。该协议也符合越日政治局第57-NQ/TW号决议和第68-NQ/TW号决议的指导方针，通过基础设施建设、资源互联和技术转让，为推进越日全面战略伙伴关系做出贡献。

在活动致辞中，斯塔维安集团董事长丁德胜先生表示： “数字基础设施是人工智能、数字经济发展和国家竞争力提升的关键基础。斯塔维安集团将与迈达斯资本及国际合作伙伴携手，开发符合国际标准的、具备互联互通和扩展能力的海底光缆基础设施项目、数据中心以及人工智能/系统集成基础设施。我们期望此次合作能够促进投资资源、技术和国际经验的对接，助力越南发展数字基础设施，推动数字化转型，并拓展与日本及区域内其他伙伴的技术合作。”

越南国会一致同意拨款 80400 亿越南盾用于 2027 年的薪酬改革。在2027年超过2.06万亿越南盾的经常性支出中，国会拨款80.4万亿越南盾用于薪酬改革。

已拨付 54.3 万亿越南盾用于支持企业和增长动力。截至 2026 年 9 月，针对中小企业和经济增长驱动因素的信贷计划已向 30,000 名客户发放了 54.3 万亿越南盾，与常规贷款利率相比，普通利率降低了 1-2%。

通过与 Midas Capital 的合作以及 MViSTA 和 Stavian DP 项目的开发，Stavian 集团不断扩大其在技术和基础设施领域的业务，与集团的四大支柱：工业、技术、能源和贸易保持一致，旨在为越南的数字化转型和高科技生态系统的发展做出贡献。
